A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work, retaining its research questions, human benchmarks, and information-theoretic framework. The text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support reliable matching across versions.

before.justification: v3 reports original embedding-clustering measurements, typicality correlations, and compression–distortion analyses against human categorization data in Section 5 and the appendices.

after.justification: v4 retains original empirical analyses and adds contextual representation results, training trajectories, prompt/pooling comparisons, lexical audits, and an analysis relating L to MMLU scores.

M1.justification: v4 adds a contextual representation-extraction variant to v3's static E-matrix pipeline, using prompted item/category text and pooled hidden states. The k-means comparison framework and L objective remain unchanged.

E1.justification: The three English human categorization datasets and their core tasks remain unchanged. v4 extends the input scenarios to controlled prompt contexts and adds an analysis using MMLU scores for instruction-tuned models (Appendix A.14). The added CLIP encoders are evaluated on text.

E2.justification: v4 adds Word2Vec, GloVe, CLIP text encoders, GPT-2, and OLMo to reported comparisons. T5 already appeared in v3's clustering table but gains typicality results in v4. Comparator membership also changes within typicality comparisons: for example, Qwen1.5-72B appears in v3 Table 2 but is absent from v4 Tables 3–4.

E3.justification: The main AMI comparison changes from static embeddings to peak-over-layer contextual AMI, with the selected layer also used for contextual typicality. New protocols compare eight prompts and four pooling strategies across eight models, examine 57 OLMo checkpoints, and analyze 13 instruction-tuned models alongside MMLU scores.

E4.justification: Appendices A.3–A.7 add prompt/pooling sensitivity, static-versus-contextual comparisons, training-development trajectories, and audits of potential polysemy and tokenizer confounds. Appendix A.14 newly examines whether compression relates to downstream performance. These substantially expand the questions investigated beyond v3's supplementary clustering and typicality analyses.

E5.justification: Appendix A.14 adds a separate significance assessment for the L–MMLU association, reporting p = 0.508. Both versions retain 100 random k-means initializations and p < 0.05 typicality significance reporting; no increase in repeated runs is documented.

E6.justification: v4 adds contextual AMI, typicality, and L results, training trajectories, and L–MMLU results. Existing static typicality values also change: BERT-large on Rosch (1973) changes from -0.427 in v3 Table 2 to 0.378 in v4 Table 3, without an explained processing or sign-convention revision. The 99-row static clustering table is unchanged, while entropy curves are removed.

T1.justification: Equations 1–4 retain the same complexity, distortion, and combined objective definitions. The extreme-case derivations move from v3 Appendix A.7 to v4 A.12 without mathematical changes; deleting an editorial placeholder does not alter the theory.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the framework and dataset-release contributions, broad categorical alignment, limited typicality fidelity, and divergent compression strategies. The expanded experiments support the existing headline claims without redefining them.

C2.justification: v4 adds explanations involving layer-specific categorical versus typicality organization, training-driven redistribution of semantic processing, and representation-learning objectives. It also argues that polysemy/tokenization cannot explain the findings and that L captures a property orthogonal to benchmark accuracy. The static-only limitation is removed.

D1.justification: v4 newly documents the default prompt including its trailing space, token-pooling alternatives, contextual category-label substitution, checkpoint schedules, WordNet exclusions, and vocabulary cleanup for tokenizer overlap. These substantially expand reproducibility information. The dataset CSV access information remains unchanged.

R1.justification: References for OLMo, GPT-2, CLIP, Word2Vec, GloVe, and T5 are added alongside the expanded model comparisons. Section 2's related-work discussion, identified research gap, and overall novelty positioning remain unchanged.

P1.justification: The main section order and much of the abstract, introduction, theory, and conclusion are retained. Changes include localized expansions in Sections 3 and 5, inserted appendix subsections, an additional author and contact details, and removal of an editorial placeholder. The underlying narrative structure remains stable.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is redrawn for peak AMI; Figure 2 replaces the entropy panel with distortion-versus-complexity and displays contextual L. v4 adds pooling/prompt plots, heatmaps, training trajectories, and separate static/contextual typicality displays. Entropy figures disappear, while existing NMI/ARI plots and the static clustering table are relocated.

improvement.justification: Contextual analyses, classic embedding baselines, and prompt/pooling controls strengthen evidence beyond v3's static-only comparisons. The net gain is limited by unexplained changes in static typicality correlations, retained references to removed entropy plots, and interpreting the nonsignificant L–MMLU association as evidence of orthogonality. The revision improves empirical scrutiny but leaves consequential reporting and interpretation problems.
